To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peak power-to-mas and peak mass-to power indices are new variables that may be calculated from the data obtained during quantitative stress echocardiographic studies.
the peak power-to-mas ratio is an index of myocardial efficiency, and that the peak mass-to-power is a measure of myocardial hypertrophy.
peak power-to-mas and peak mass-to-pwer are variables that couple LV mass and power output and may be useful in the assessment of cardiac dynamics and in the prediction of clinical outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of peak power output-to-mass ratio and peak mass-to-output ratio in patients with LV disease.
the development and application of new echocardiographic techniques for assessing cardiac dynamics in patients with coronary heart disease and LV systolic dysfunction.
the development of new indices that may provide a more comprehensive assessment of the cardiac performance and may help to distinguish the compensatory from the maladaptive remodeling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assessment of peak cardiac power output-to-mass ratio is an interesting new tool for the evaluation of cardiac function and for the prognostic assessment of LV systolic dysfunction.
the assessment of peak power output-to-mass and mass-to-power ratios may be a useful tool to identify patients with a high risk of adverse cardiac events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peak power-to-masses and peak mass-to-powers are useful indices to identify patients with LV dysfunction and coronary artery stenoses that have a high risk for major cardiovascular events.
peak power-to-mas is a powerful prognostic index in patients with LV hypertrophy or LV dysfunction and it can be used to identify the presence and severity of cardiac disease.
peak power-to-mas is an index of the ability of the heart to deliver energy to the periphery and peak mass-to-pwer is an index of myocardial energy storage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peak power-to-mas may be a more sensitive index than peak mass-to-power for detecting the transition between compensated and decompensated LV remodeling in patients with heart failure.
the peak power-to-mas ratio and peak mass-to-peak power ratio are useful indices to assess myocardial energy balance during stress echocardography.
